title: Particles in solids, liquids and gases
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:22Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T15:15:52Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The bank point on solids, liquids and gases matches the packing and compressibility ideas, but the new point also teaches that particles attract each other, which that card never covers, and the separate particle theory point covers only part of the combined idea.

draft.title: Particles in solids, liquids and gases
card: All matter is made of tiny particles that are always moving. The particles attract each other.
the particles are packed closely in a fixed pattern. They vibrate on the spot but do not move past each other, so a solid keeps its shape and volume.
the particles are close together but not in a fixed pattern. They slide past each other, so a liquid flows and takes the shape of its container.
the particles are far apart and move freely in all directions. The attraction between them is very weak, so a gas spreads out to fill its container and can be squashed into a smaller space.
draft.remember: Particles are always moving. Packing and freedom to move decide whether matter is a solid, liquid or gas.

a.q: Why can a gas be squashed into a smaller volume, while a solid cannot?
opts: Gas particles are far apart, so they can be pushed closer
Gas particles are smaller than solid particles
Gas particles do not move, so they can be moved
Gas particles are packed in a fixed pattern
a.why: Gas particles have a lot of empty space between them, so they can be pushed closer together. Solid particles are already packed closely. The size of the particles does not change between states.
a.clue: Think about the space between the particles.

b.q: Sam pours water from a jug into a tall glass. The water changes shape but is still the same amount. Which idea about its particles explains this?
opts: They are close together but slide past each other
They are fixed in a pattern and only vibrate
They are far apart and fill the whole glass
They stop moving and settle at the bottom
b.why: Liquid particles stay close together, so the volume stays the same. They can slide past each other, so the water takes the shape of the glass. Particles in a fixed pattern would make a solid, which keeps its shape.
b.clue: The amount stays the same, but the shape can change.

wants.brief: Three boxes side by side labelled Solid, Liquid and Gas. Solid: particles drawn as circles packed closely in a regular pattern. Liquid: circles close together in a random arrangement, touching or nearly touching. Gas: a few circles far apart, with small arrows showing movement in different directions.
wants.why: Seeing the packing and spacing of particles side by side helps students link each state to its properties.

a.best: Gas particles are far apart, so they can be pushed closer

b.best: They are close together but slide past each other
